questions.question_text:
What will be logged to the console by the following code?
console.log(1); setTimeout(() => console.log(2), 0); Promise.resolve().then(() => console.log(3)); console.log(4);
questions.explanation: Synchronous operations run first (1, 4). Microtasks like Promise.then() run before Macrotasks like setTimeout(..., 0), yielding 1, 4, 3, 2.

questions.question_text: Which TypeScript utility type constructs a type with all properties of Type set to optional?
questions.explanation: Partial<Type> creates a new type containing all properties of Type marked as optional.

questions.question_text: What does a JavaScript closure primarily allow an inner function to do?
questions.option_a: Execute in a multi-threaded web worker automatically
questions.option_b: Access variables from its outer (enclosing) lexical scope even after that scope has finished executing
questions.option_c: Prevent all garbage collection of the entire window object
questions.option_d: Convert synchronous callback functions into WebAssembly bytecode
questions.explanation: A closure gives a function access to its outer scope variables from an inner function, preserved across invocations.

questions.question_text: What is the output of `typeof null` in standard JavaScript?
questions.explanation: In JavaScript, typeof null evaluates to "object" due to an infamous legacy design quirk dating back to the first JS implementation in 1995.

questions.question_text: Which method creates a new array with all sub-array elements concatenated recursively up to a specified depth?
questions.explanation: Array.prototype.flat(depth) flattens nested arrays to the specified depth (defaulting to 1).

questions.question_text: What is the purpose of the `unknown` type in TypeScript compared to `any`?
questions.option_a: unknown allows assigning to any type without type checking
questions.option_b: unknown is type-safe: you cannot invoke methods or access properties on it without narrowing or assertion first
questions.option_c: unknown is identical to never and can never hold a runtime value
questions.option_d: unknown only permits null or undefined values
questions.explanation: unknown is the type-safe counterpart of any. Operations on unknown require type narrowing or assertions beforehand.

questions.question_text: Why must unique and stable `key` props be provided when rendering a dynamic list in React?
questions.option_a: Keys are sent to CSS selectors to style each list item uniquely
questions.option_b: Keys enable React reconciliation to identify which items have changed, been added, or removed efficiently
questions.option_c: Keys prevent components from unmounting even when removed from the DOM
questions.option_d: Keys allow children components to modify parent props directly
questions.explanation: React uses keys to match existing children in the Virtual DOM tree with new children during reconciliation.

questions.question_text: Which hook should you use to cache the result of an expensive calculation between re-renders?
questions.explanation: useMemo caches the result of a calculation between renders unless its dependencies change. (useCallback caches function definitions).

questions.question_text: Which HTTP status code signifies that a requested resource was created successfully on the server?
questions.explanation: HTTP 201 Created indicates that the request has succeeded and resulted in the creation of a new resource.

questions.question_text: What happens when `useRef` value is updated (e.g. `ref.current = newValue`)?
questions.option_b: The component re-renders asynchronously on the next tick
questions.option_c: The value changes without triggering a component re-render
questions.option_d: An error is thrown unless wrapped in startTransition
questions.explanation: Updating a ref is a pure mutation of its current property and does not notify React or trigger a re-render.

questions.question_text: What does CORS (Cross-Origin Resource Sharing) protect against?
questions.option_a: SQL injection on the backend database
questions.option_b: Malicious websites making unauthorized read requests to another domain using the user's browser credentials
questions.option_c: Denial of Service attacks by rate limiting user IP addresses
questions.option_d: Client-side memory leaks in Single Page Applications
questions.explanation: CORS is a browser security mechanism that restricts resources requested from another origin to prevent unauthorized cross-origin reading.

questions.question_text: What does the "I" stand for in ACID database transaction properties?
questions.explanation: ACID stands for Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, and Durability.

questions.question_text: What is the primary difference between a WHERE clause and a HAVING clause in SQL?
questions.option_a: WHERE filters rows after aggregation; HAVING filters rows before aggregation
questions.option_b: WHERE filters individual rows before grouping; HAVING filters aggregated groups after GROUP BY
questions.option_c: WHERE only works on numeric columns; HAVING works on string columns
questions.option_d: WHERE can only be used with SELECT; HAVING can be used with UPDATE
questions.explanation: WHERE filters rows before aggregation occurs, while HAVING filters aggregated results (like COUNT, SUM) after GROUP BY.

questions.question_text: Which Normal Form requires that every non-key attribute must be non-transitively dependent on the primary key?
questions.explanation: 3NF requires that the table is in 2NF and that all attributes are directly dependent on the primary key, eliminating transitive dependencies.

questions.question_text: What data structure is most commonly utilized by relational database engines for B-Tree indexes?
questions.explanation: Most relational databases (PostgreSQL, MySQL InnoDB, SQLite) use B+ Trees because leaf nodes form a linked list, optimizing sequential range scans.

questions.question_text: What will a `LEFT JOIN` return when a row in the left table has no matching row in the right table?
questions.option_a: The row is omitted from the result set
questions.option_b: The row is returned with NULL values for the right table columns
questions.option_c: A runtime foreign key constraint violation is raised
questions.option_d: The query hangs until a timeout occurs
questions.explanation: A LEFT JOIN returns all records from the left table, and the matched records from the right table; if no match exists, NULL values are filled.

questions.question_text: What is the average time complexity of searching for an element in a balanced Binary Search Tree (AVL or Red-Black)?
questions.explanation: In a balanced binary search tree, the height is logarithmic (log2 n), making lookup, insertion, and deletion O(log n).

questions.question_text: Which algorithm is best suited for finding the shortest path from a single source node in a graph with non-negative edge weights?
questions.explanation: Dijkstra's algorithm finds the shortest paths between nodes in a graph with non-negative edge weights in O((V + E) log V) with a priority queue.

questions.question_text: Which data structure operates on a First-In, First-Out (FIFO) principle?
questions.explanation: A Queue operates under FIFO (First-In, First-Out). Stacks operate under LIFO (Last-In, First-Out).

questions.question_text: What is a "Deadlock" condition in operating systems?
questions.option_a: When CPU clock speed exceeds the maximum rated thermal capacity
questions.option_b: A state where two or more processes are unable to proceed because each is waiting for the other to release a resource
questions.option_c: When hard drive sectors become permanently corrupted
questions.option_d: When a network packet repeatedly circles a routing loop until TTL expires
questions.explanation: Deadlock happens when a set of concurrent processes are blocked because each process is holding a resource and waiting for another held by another process.

questions.question_text: What is the worst-case time complexity of QuickSort?
questions.explanation: QuickSort has an average complexity of O(n log n), but degrades to O(n^2) when an unbalanced partition is repeatedly chosen (e.g. sorted array with first element as pivot).

questions.question_text: What is the primary fundamental difference between a Docker container and a Virtual Machine (VM)?
questions.option_a: Containers virtualize hardware; VMs share the host kernel
questions.option_b: Containers share the host OS kernel and isolate at process level, while VMs run full guest operating systems on a hypervisor
questions.option_c: Containers can only execute compiled C++ binaries
questions.option_d: VMs do not require RAM or storage allocations
questions.explanation: Containers share the host operating system kernel and run as isolated processes, making them significantly lighter and faster than VMs.

questions.question_text: In Kubernetes, what is the smallest deployable computing unit that can be created and managed?
questions.explanation: A Pod is the smallest execution unit in Kubernetes, encapsulating one or more containers sharing network and storage.

questions.question_text: What does a Reverse Proxy (such as Nginx or Envoy) do?
questions.option_a: Sits between clients and origin servers to handle routing, SSL termination, caching, and load balancing
questions.option_b: Allows employees inside a corporate LAN to access the external internet anonymously
questions.option_c: Decrypts database files stored on disk
questions.option_d: Acts as a compiler for client-side JavaScript bundles
questions.explanation: A reverse proxy sits in front of web servers and forwards client requests to those servers, handling SSL termination, load balancing, and security.

questions.question_text: Which DNS record type maps a hostname directly to an IPv4 address?
questions.explanation: An "A" (Address) record maps a domain name to an IPv4 address. (AAAA maps to IPv6).
